video.title: Board of Trustees of the Affordable Housing Trust (AHT) 8/26/26

summary.headline: Affordable Housing Trust advances 55-plus zoning bylaw revisions, plans town survey questions, and explores new funding sources.
summary.summary: The Southborough Affordable Housing Trust discussed drafting housing-related questions for the town's upcoming annual community survey, focusing on housing types, senior needs, and potential locations. Members reviewed updates to a proposed 55-plus housing bylaw revision that would remove unit caps and establish a 12.5 percent affordability requirement for spring 2025 Town Meeting. The board also examined funding options, including developer mitigation fees, Community Preservation Act grants, and higher investment yields for its $1 million fund balance. In addition, the trust coordinated a state technical assistance grant application and entered executive session to discuss potential land acquisitions.

topics.title: Routine business
topics.summary: The board reviewed and approved the open meeting minutes from July 20, 2024, with minor typographical corrections. Members also voted to approve and release executive session minutes from July 20, 2024, and release executive session minutes from April 9, April 14, and May 22, 2024, which pertained to Chapter 61A land on Northborough Road.
key_details: Approved open meeting minutes for July 20, 2024, by a 4-0-1 vote.
Voted 5-0 to release executive session minutes from April 9, April 14, May 22, and July 20, 2024.
Released minutes relate to prior town discussions regarding Chapter 61A property on Northborough Road.
topics.outcome: Open meeting minutes approved and executive session minutes released for public inspection.

topics.title: Annual community survey housing questions
topics.summary: The board discussed submitting questions to the town's annual community survey conducted by the Municipal Technology Committee. Members agreed to focus on housing typologies, demographic needs such as senior and municipal workforce housing, and potential locations along Route 9, downtown, or near the MBTA station. The board decided to exclude questions regarding a real estate transfer fee, determining the topic requires extensive public education first.
key_details: Questions will cover housing styles including single-family homes, townhomes, cottages, multi-family units, and accessory dwelling units.
Survey options will assess community needs for 55-plus residents, municipal employees, and downsizing opportunities.
Geographic preference options will include Route 9, downtown, MBTA transit areas, and dispersed neighborhood sites.
Members decided against surveying on a real estate transfer fee to avoid negative sentiment prior to formal public outreach.
The chair will draft the proposed questions and circulate them for individual member review.
topics.outcome: The chair will draft specific survey questions and gather member feedback to finalize the submission.

topics.title: Mini-Boost technical assistance grant application
topics.summary: Members reviewed the status of an application for a Mini-Boost grant to receive state technical assistance for affordable housing planning. The application seeks consulting support to build local capacity and formulate housing strategies and financing frameworks. The chair requested a necessary letter of support from the Select Board and agreed to share past application documents with board members to finalize the filing.
key_details: The Mini-Boost grant provides technical consulting assistance rather than direct cash funding.
Requested assistance focuses on project planning capacity, housing strategy, and financial modeling.
The application requires an official letter of support from the Select Board.
The chair submitted a letter request to the Select Board and will coordinate draft text with trust members.
topics.outcome: The chair will share past application materials and work with members to finalize and submit the application.

topics.title: 55-plus housing bylaw revisions
topics.summary: The board discussed proposed amendments to the town's 55-plus housing bylaw ahead of the spring 2025 Town Meeting following consultations with the Zoning Board of Appeals and the town planner. The revision intends to remove the existing townwide cap on senior housing units while establishing a minimum 12.5 percent affordability mandate. Members also considered adding a minimum lot size requirement, such as two acres, to moderate density and address neighborhood impacts under special permits.
key_details: Working to remove the total unit cap in the existing 55-plus housing bylaw.
Proposing a mandatory 12.5 percent affordability requirement for new 55-plus developments.
Discussing a potential minimum lot size of two acres to manage neighborhood density impacts.
Current base density under consideration is six units per acre via special permit.
Members noted recent changes in state law that lowered the threshold for residential use variances.
topics.outcome: Working group members will consult Town Counsel and present a revised draft bylaw at the next meeting.
topics.why_it_matters: Amending the 55-plus bylaw would lift restrictions on the number of senior housing units permitted in town and establish new affordability mandates for future developments.

topics.title: Funding strategies and property acquisition review
topics.summary: The board discussed potential funding mechanisms for the trust, including advocating for developer mitigation fees and exploring higher-yield investment options for its existing funds. Members agreed to approach the Select Board to request that developer mitigation fees from projects be deposited into the housing trust. The board also agreed to submit an annual application for Community Preservation Act housing funds and reviewed privately owned parcels of 30 to 40 acres across town for potential negotiated acquisition, donation, or eminent domain.
key_details: Trust holds approximately $1 million in cash reserves, recently supplemented by an annual $60,000 CPA transfer.
Members proposed asking the Select Board to allocate developer mitigation fees, citing past examples like Madison Place, to the housing trust.
The board will inquire with the town treasurer regarding options to improve interest yields on trust fund balances.
The trust will prepare an application for the upcoming Community Preservation Act funding cycle.
A review of assessor records identified approximately six large private parcels to evaluate for potential acquisition.
topics.outcome: Members will request an agenda item with the Select Board regarding developer fees, prepare a CPA application, and review parcel details in executive session.
topics.why_it_matters: Securing dedicated developer mitigation fees and CPA grants directly affects municipal resources available to fund affordable housing projects in Southborough.
